ops.title: The dense retrieval lane is dropped and Phase 0 is cancelled
ops.body:
Owner decision 2026-07-27, superseding "hold the dense lane built but unshipped"
in doc `3d9c793`.

## What happened

Phase 0 — extracting cc-context's `semsearch`/`cache`/`embed`/`rank` (~1,700 LOC)
into a shared Go module — was built and deliberately held. It lived as
**uncommitted** changes in a worktree under `/tmp/ccn-exec/P0/wt`. `/tmp` was
purged. There is no dangling commit and no stash: both P0 worktrees still point at
their base `a222707` and their reflogs have a single entry each. The work is gone.

## Why it is not being rebuilt

The measurements taken since it was parked do not support the cost:

- **S1**: dense-only loses to BM25 on every category. RRF fusion wins on exactly one
  — conceptual paraphrase, +0.181 NDCG, p=0.002. Dense also had to embed title+tags
  rather than the body, because static mean-pooling dilutes with length.
- **P2** (note `1bb5e4ff`): the shipped ranker — lexical BM25 + identifier enrichment
  + PPR graph lane, **no dense lane at all** — measures NDCG@10 0.877 / recall 0.981
  against BM25's 0.817. There is very little headroom left for dense to claim, and
  what remains is not where it helps.

Rebuilding 1,700 LOC of extraction, a forked golden-parity suite and a second copy
of the model pins, to chase one question category, is not a trade worth making.

## Consequences

1. `kg.Embedder`, `kg.Options.Embedder`, `attachVectors` and `Node.Vector` are dead
   code and are removed — nothing implements the interface and nothing will.
2. **Phase D's justification is void.** The daemon's measured case was
   `em_load_model` at 133 ms, 79% of warm engine init, amortizable only by a
   resident process. With no engine there is no such cost. The daemon must be
   re-justified from scratch against `internal/kg/index.go`, which already persists
   the graph to bbolt keyed by a source digest: if `kg.Load` plus one query is
   single-digit milliseconds, a hook reads the index directly and the daemon
   collapses to a writer — or is not needed at all.
3. The wasm-at-runtime pin, the `HF_ENDPOINT` mirror path and the
   hardened-runtime/entitlement analysis all become moot for cc-notes. They remain
   correct for cc-context.

## The process lesson

"Hold it built" was implemented as "leave it uncommitted in a `/tmp` worktree", and
that is not holding anything — it is a countdown. Held work gets a commit on a
branch, or it does not exist. Nothing else in wave 1–3 was lost, because everything
else had been committed.
